From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt ingestion & canary schedule — Acme

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for sending the first batch. Two quick asks to make the canary run smoother:

1) If you can add a simple "rubric" column with pass/partial/fail guidance for expected summaries that would help our automated checks.
2) For non-English snippets, can you add a language tag (e.g. "es") in a language column. We'll run those separately so we can measure degradation by language.

We're ready to validate the file as soon as you upload V2. Marcus/Dylan, if the file looks good I'll hand it over to you for ingestion and scheduling.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Ramos <miguel.ramos@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt ingestion & canary schedule — Acme

Hi Marissa,

Thanks 5 for the guidance 5 we uploaded acme_prompts_v2.csv to the shared Drive link and attached it here. Notes on V2:

- ~310 rows, includes rubric column (pass/partial/fail) and language column for non-English.
- Kept order ids as ORD-XXXXX consistently.
- Redacted personal names to [NAME_REDACTED]; we left some long threads unredacted but flagged them in the PII column for manual review.
- Edge cases: mixed-html rows flagged with strip_html=true; multi-intent rows flagged in edge_case_notes.

Let us know if any rows need manual unredaction or if you'd prefer encrypted transfer for sensitive examples.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Operations, Acme Corp
samantha.ortiz@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt ingestion & canary schedule — Acme

Perfect  thanks Samantha. Two clarifications before ingestion:

- For the rows flagged PII: yes please keep them redacted and flagged. If there are any rows you want us to test unredacted, we can accept up to 25 via an encrypted transfer and will follow your security checklist.
- For mixed-language rows: we'll separate by language and run the same canary models per language. If Spanish performance is critical, please flag those as high-priority.

Marcus/Dylan: once Marcus validates the CSV schema, please run automated redaction checks and report any rows that fail validation. Dylan, can you tentatively schedule the canary for Monday 6/22 and allocate the human review sample (n=50)?

Thanks all,
Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt ingestion & canary schedule — Acme

Update: I validated acme_prompts_v2.csv against the prompt_ingestion_checklist.md this morning. Results:

- Schema OK: all required columns present (prompt_text, expected_summary, rubric, PII, edge_case_notes, language, strip_html).
- Automated redaction checks: 6 rows flagged for potential unredacted emails/order patterns; I flagged those for manual review and added comments in the Drive file.
- Ingestion: prepping the dataset now and will hand off to Dylan by end of day today.

Dylan please confirm you can start the canary on 2026-06-22. We'll run the three model variants (fast-7b-v2 quantized; tt-13b fp16; opt-6.7b) and hold out the 50-row human review sample as discussed. I expect initial metrics (ROUGE, hallucination rate) by 2026-06-25.

Marcus Lin
